text:
- [LCDB.3.2.3] **An on-delay is a `where` condition, not a modifier.** A
  rule that must fire only once a match has held for `T` states it on the
  matched fact, as `where x.dwell >= T` on a `logical` binding ([LEXP.9.5.1]).
  The condition is time-dependent, so the engine re-evaluates it on every pump
  ([LTIM.2.4.2]) and fires on the pump at which it first holds ([LTIM.2.5.1]).
  If the fact is retracted or replaced before `T` has passed, the match ends
  and nothing fires. The engine keeps no rate state for it; the rule header
  has no on-delay modifier ([LCDB.5.1]).

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__on_delay
idris.note: THE ON-DELAY as the clause writes it: `where x.dwell >= T` on the matched fact, `T` 2 here. A fixture.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__on_delay_fires_once
idris.note: THE ON-DELAY FIRES ONCE, AT THE FIRST PUMP WHOSE SAMPLE REACHES T, AND NEVER AGAIN: a Motion asserted at 0 under `dwell >= 2`; the pump at 0 fires nothing, the pump at 3 fires, the pump at 6 does not -- logical/LCDB.3.2.3_dwell_on_delay's shape. Executed through the loader, the stamps and the gated pump: `[[], [(0, True)], []]`.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__retracted_before_t_fires_nothing
idris.note: 'If the fact is retracted or replaced before T has passed, the match ends and nothing fires': the Motion asserted at 0, retracted at 1, the pump at 3 -- logical/LCDB.3.2.3_dwell_on_delay_retracted's shape. Executed: `[[]]`.
